title: Cost of the LCFs' meaning: how much of the seven LCFs the TD3+BC free latents hold, the arm that beat the LCFs
description: What the free latents learned in the arm that showed the cost: exp-lcf-cost-probe-324 probed only the free encoders of the clones and of expliCCit's CQL, not those of TD3+BC, whose free arm beat neto1 v1's LCF estimates by 0.46 to 0.78 (exp-lcf-cost-td3-report-329). For the TD3+BC free encoder on each of its five training seeds (lcftd-free-a2.5-n150k-sN, seeds 0 and 1 from exp-lcf-cost-td3-326, 2 to 4 from exp-lcf-cost-td3-seeds-328), two maps from the seven latents to each of neto1 v1's LCFs, in neto1 v1's target space, fitted on the training links of the policy's own split of exp-data-net2-steps-222 and scored by R^2 on its validation links, every 10th step (experiments/latent_probe.py, as in exp-lcf-cost-probe-324): a linear map with a bias, and a network with two hidden layers of 128 fitted to all seven at once. References: neto1 v1's own output (the paper arm's latents, lcftd-paper-a2.5-n60k-s0) and the free encoder with fresh weights.
run: N="$IN/n/$(cat "$IN/n/chosen.txt")/net1.pt"; A=(); for s in 0 1 2 3 4; do F="$IN/p"; [ "$s" -ge 2 ] && F="$IN/s"; A+=("lcftd-free-a2.5-n150k-s$s=$F/lcftd-free-a2.5-n150k-s$s"); done; A+=("lcftd-paper-a2.5-n60k-s0=$IN/p/lcftd-paper-a2.5-n60k-s0"); for a in "${A[@]}"; do [ -f "${a#*=}/net2.pt" ] && [ -f "${a#*=}/train_spec.json" ]; done; [ "${#A[@]}" -eq 6 ]; uv run python experiments/latent_probe.py "$OUT" "$IN/d" "$N" "${A[@]}" random=random
